text.title: constitution.md — Output Contract
text.summary: The artefact is a Markdown file, not a data structure, because it is read by humans and loaded verbatim into agent context. The contract is therefore a document shape, checked structurally by the bundled validator.

schema.code:
# <Project> Constitution
<!-- Sync Impact Report version: 0.0.0 -> 1.0.0 added: R-01..R-07 modified: - removed: - out of sync: <files whose content this change invalidates, or "-"> -->
## Scope
Domain facts, business rules, the data model, invariants and deploy topology live in `<path>/project-spec/`, not here. This file holds only standing decisions about how the work is done.
## Rules
### R-01 <short title>
**Why:** <one sentence, written before the rule>
<the rule, imperative, at most 60 words>
### R-02 <short title> ...
## Compliance
<who or what checks these rules, what happens on violation, and which rules are mechanically checked today versus checked only by reading.>
## Amendment
<how a rule is proposed, changed or retired; the semver policy from r6.>
---
**Version:** 1.0.0 · **Ratified:** 2026-08-04 · **Last amended:** 2026-08-04

list.item: f1 — more than twenty `### R-NN` blocks, or a rule body over sixty words.
f2 — a rule with no `**Why:**` line, or a why longer than one sentence.
f3 — non-sequential, duplicated or reused `R-NN` ids.
f4 — an unresolved `TODO(...)` or `[PLACEHOLDER]` in a ratified file. Permitted only while the document is explicitly a draft.
f5 — a missing or unparseable footer, or a ratified date later than the last-amended date.
f6 — a missing Scope, Rules, Compliance or Amendment section.
f7 — a Scope section that does not name a `project-spec/` location. Delegation is mandatory even when the folder is empty; "we have no domain facts yet" is a claim that ages badly.
f8 — two rules that contradict each other. Not machine-detectable; listed here so that the review has to look for it.

example.code:
### R-03 One migration per pull request
**Why:** two migrations in one PR cannot be rolled back independently, and we have already lost an evening to exactly that.
Each pull request contains at most one schema migration. A change needing two migrations is split into two pull requests, merged in order.
example.note: Durable, cross-cutting, contestable (batching migrations is a defensible choice), checkable by counting migration files in the diff — and the why names a real incident rather than a principle.

example.code:
### R-04 Code quality
**Why:** quality is important.
The team should write clean, maintainable, well-tested code and follow best practices wherever possible.
example.note: Fails three parts of the admission test at once: not contestable (nobody argues for the opposite), not checkable (no observation would show a violation), and the why is a restatement of the rule. It also contains an escape clause, "wherever possible", which makes it unenforceable by construction. This is what a constitution fills up with when there is no admission gate.

section.title: Consistency rules the validator enforces
section.statement: Rule ids are sequential from `R-01` with no gaps and no duplicates. Every rule block has a `**Why:**` line and a non-empty body. Rule count is at most twenty and each body is at most sixty words. The four sections are present. The footer parses and `Ratified` is not later than `Last amended`. In default mode no `TODO(` or `[PLACEHOLDER]` survives; `--draft` relaxes only that check. The validator does NOT and cannot check whether the rules are good, whether they contradict each other, or whether the code obeys them — see `content/03-failure-modes.xml`.

text.reference: The empty template. Passes `--draft`, fails default, which is the correct behaviour for an unfilled file.
